Exercise: Standing Calf Raises

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- ankle_plantar_flexion

Primary Muscles:

- calves

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- machine

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- posture_improvement
- calf_hypertrophy

Contraindications:

- condition: Recent Ankle Surgery, description: Avoid this exercise if you have recently undergone ankle surgery. Consult your healthcare provider before resuming any calf exercises.
- condition: Severe Achilles Tendonitis, description: If you are experiencing severe pain or inflammation in the Achilles tendon, avoid this exercise and consult a medical professional for appropriate treatment.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Toes Out/In Standing Calf Raises, instructions: ['Adjust the padded lever of the calf raise machine to fit your height.', 'Place your shoulders under the pads provided and position your toes facing outward or inward as described at the beginning of the chapter. The balls of your feet should be secured on top of the calf block with the heels extending off it. Push the lever up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is standing erect. The knees should be kept with a slight bend; never locked.', 'Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calves. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position for a second before you start to go back down.', 'Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.', 'Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.']

Substitution Options:

- name: Seated Calf Raises, equipment: machine
- name: Bodyweight Calf Raises, equipment: bodyweight

Instructions:

- Adjust the padded lever of the calf raise machine to fit your height.
- Place your shoulders under the pads provided and position your toes facing forward (or using any of the two other positions described at the beginning of the chapter). The balls of your feet should be secured on top of the calf block with the heels extending off it. Push the lever up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is standing erect. The knees should be kept with a slight bend; never locked. Toes should be facing forward, outwards or inwards as described at the beginning of the chapter. This will be your starting position.
- Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
- Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
